# kui-player

> A video player chrome you can put on any `<video>` element — including one a page
> already owns. Vanilla TypeScript core plus a React subpath, ~26 kB gzipped, **zero
> runtime dependencies**, no CSS framework, no icon font, and no network request other
> than the media you point it at.

kui-player is not trying to be a general-purpose player framework. It is the controls
layer: accessible, themeable through CSS custom properties, and mountable over a
`<video>` that some other pipeline (progressive, hls.js, MSE, blob) is already feeding.

- Package: `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player` (npm, Apache-2.0, ESM only)
- Entry points: `.` (vanilla core), `./react`, `./skin`, `./locales`, `./wrappers/vue`, `./wrappers/svelte`, `./styles.css`
- Requires React 18/19 only for the `./react` subpath; the core has no framework
- Vue, Svelte, Angular and plain HTML are served by wrappers or `<kui-player>`

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/blob/main/README.md): install, props, theming, streaming, accessibility, bundle budgets
- [llms-full.txt](https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/blob/main/llms-full.txt): the complete API surface, types and recipes in one file
- [Recipes](https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/tree/main/recipes): copy-pasteable integrations (Next.js, Vite, WordPress, skin mode, hls.js, analytics)
- [Wrappers](https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/tree/main/wrappers): Vue, Svelte and the custom element
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the rules a change has to satisfy
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/tree/main/phases): what is built, what is next, and why

## The three ways to use it

- **React component** — `<VideoPlayer src="…" />` from `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/react`. Client boundary is declared for the Next.js App Router.
- **Vanilla engine** — `new VideoPlayerEngine()` then `engine.attach(videoElement)`; drives a Zustand vanilla store you can subscribe to.
- **Skin mode** — one `<script>` tag dresses videos the page already has: `<script src="…/dist/embed.js" data-auto="video"></script>`. No build step, no markup change.

## What else it does

- Chapters and seek-preview storyboards from WebVTT sidecars
- Playlists with a cancellable "up next" card
- Live streams with a DVR window and a LIVE badge
- SRT and ASS subtitles, plus caption colour/background/edge/font controls
- OS media controls (Media Session), AirPlay, Picture-in-Picture, Google Cast with queues
- Six languages with RTL layout, and localised durations
- A local analytics API: quartiles, rebuffers, startup time, time to first frame
- Resume-where-you-left-off, off by default

## What it deliberately does not do

- Ship an HLS or DASH engine. Bring `hls.js` or `dash.js` and pass an adapter; nothing is bundled for apps that do not stream.
- Send telemetry, load fonts, or fetch icons. It has no runtime dependencies at all. Google Cast is the one external request, it is opt-in, and a CI test enforces the rest.
- Impose styling. One scoped stylesheet, every class prefixed `kui-`, themed with `--kui-*` custom properties.
